newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA COURT TO RULE ON FP BANK BY MID-JULY.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA COURT TO RULE ON FP BANK BY MID-JULY.

text.p: Bulgaria's Supreme Court will rule by mid-July on a central bank appeal against a lower court's rejection of an insolvency claim against First Private Bank (FPB), a central bank official said on Wednesday.
"The Supreme Court will announce its decision whether the (central bank) appeal is justified by the middle of July," the official told reporters.
FPB officials were not immediately available for comment.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) put FPB, Bulgaria's biggest private bank, in receivership on May 17, 1996 and sought its insolvency through the Sofia City Court two weeks later.

But the court rejected the BNB claim in December, saying it was not supported by enough evidence. The BNB appealed against that ruling and the Supreme Court was expected to consider the appeal next month.

The central bank retracted FPB's banking licence last month, citing its failure to collect loans and repay debts of over 200 billion levs to its major creditors during the one-year period of receivership.
The BNB has said that FPB owed over 100 billion levs to the state for repayments to depositors, and over 90 billion levs to the BNB at end-March.

The FPB had a heavily negative capital to risk assets ratio and its registered capital of two billion levs was not fully paid in, which prevented possibilities for attracting potential investors to increase the FPB capital, the BNB has said.

Under a $657 million reform and funding agreement with the IMF, Bulgarian banks should have a minimum six percent capital to risk assets ratio by the end of this year and eight percent by mid-1998 to comply with international standards. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 91188
